second.derivation:
I re-read every passage in the spec file rather than trusting the packet. All eleven of the packet's substantive quotes are VERBATIM ACCURATE (I diffed them). Two citation defects and three substantive gaps follow below, but none flips the classification.

STEP 1 — The counter-reading, stated at its strongest. GR2's protasis has two conjuncts. A competent implementor could read conjunct (i), "the length of the string is specified in the rules for the context in which the figurative constant is used," as demanding that some statement-local rule EXPLICITLY state a length. §12.4.5.6 contains no such rule. On that reading GR2 fails, GR3's protasis (the exact negation) is satisfied, GR3b fires, and the answer is one character. This is the reading the packet must defeat, and the packet defeats it only by asserting that conjunct (i) "means" the context supplies a length. That assertion is under-supported as the packet argues it.

STEP 2 — I defeated it with evidence the packet never found. I searched the ENTIRE §14.9.25 MOVE section for any rule specifying a figurative constant's length. There is none. MOVE's rules address only category (SR5, SR6, SR7, Table 17) and, for numeric receivers, defer explicitly: "the figurative constant is replicated in this item, from left to right, as described in the rules for figurative constants." So MOVE — the single most canonical figurative context, and NOTE 1's first exemplar — has no statement-local length rule. Under the strict counter-reading, MOVE SPACES TO PIC X(4) would fall to GR3b and produce one space, and MOVE HIGH-VALUES TO PIC X(4) would produce 0xFF followed by three spaces. That is contrary to §8.3.3.6.4 GR2's own text (which names the VALUE clause and "association" as its scope), to NOTE 1's placement, and to universal COBOL behavior in all four editions. The strict reading renders GR2 a null set — no context anywhere would satisfy conjunct (i). Under the ordinary construction canon that no rule is surplusage, conjunct (i) must mean "the context supplies a length," and conjuncts (i)+(ii) are jointly, not independently, discriminating. This is what independently convinced me — not the packet's reasoning, which stopped at NOTE 1.

STEP 3 — NOTE 1's placement is structural, not merely lexical. I verified in the source that NOTE 1 sits between GR2 and GR3 (lines 6381 vs 6383). Notes attach to the rule they follow. The committee placed "compared with it" under the FILL rule. Correspondingly, GR3's three sub-rules (a concatenation, b non-ALL, c length of literal-1) make no reference to any receiver at all — GR3 is textually the receiver-less residue.

STEP 4 — The predicate is satisfied here. §12.4.5.6.4 GR6 states the test as "the value of data-name-1 or record-key-name-1 in that record is equal to literal-1." REWRITE GR24 and WRITE GR35 both confirm it is a relation-condition comparison. SR3 guarantees the item is fixed-length. §12.4.5.6.4 GR2 fixes record-key-name-1's length as the concatenation of all data-name-2 occurrences. GR2's predicate holds on its face; GR3 is inapplicable by its own protasis.

STEP 5 — Reductio, independently checked against Annex D. Annex D (line 41982, verified inside the Annex D span 41920–49011) says the phrase "allows suppression of records that match a literal," and Annex E item 42 (line 50336, inside 49011–50351) says suppression applies "when the value of this key equals the value specified in this phrase." Both describe whole-key value equality. Under GR3b, SUPPRESS WHEN HIGH-VALUE on a PIC X(4) key would fail to suppress an all-0xFF key — the canonical case — and would instead suppress a key of 0xFF plus three spaces. I confirmed no Annex D worked example uses a figurative as literal-1, so no annex contradicts GR2; both corroborate.

DEFECTS I FOUND IN THE PACKET (none flips the verdict):

(a) CITATION ERROR. The packet attributes GR24 to "12.4.5.6.4." §12.4.5.6.4 has exactly six general rules (lines 15364–15378). GR24 is §14.9.35 REWRITE GR24 (line 30685). The quoted text is correct; the section number is not. Must be fixed before this citation lands in code comments (project rule: cited § must MATCH).

(b) MISSED RULES. The packet cites only the REWRITE side. §14.9.51 WRITE GR41 is the WRITE-side suppression rule, and WRITE GR35 — "The comparison used for ensuring uniqueness, for ordering records, or for SUPPRESSING RECORDS in the physical file is based on the collating sequence for the file according to the rules for a relation condition" — is the single cleanest statement in the standard that suppression is a relation-condition comparison. It corroborates the packet's conclusion; the packet simply did not find it.

(c) SUBSTANTIVE ERROR IN THE IMPLEMENTATION CONSEQUENCE. The packet's item 5 says §8.8.4.2.7(2) "is unreachable and should be an assert, not a code path." That is WRONG in general. SR7 constrains literal-1's CATEGORY but imposes NO length requirement on a non-figurative literal-1 (the one-character rule applies only to ALL literal). SUPPRESS WHEN "AB" on a PIC X(4) key is therefore legal and genuinely unequal-length, and §8.8.4.2.7(2) space-extension is the governing and REACHABLE semantics for it (key "AB  " suppressed). Asserting on the padding branch would be a live defect. The correct statement is narrower: for a FIGURATIVE literal-1, GR2 makes the operands equal-length by construction so padding never arises; for an ordinary literal, padding remains live.

(d) COLLATING-SEQUENCE CONFLATION. The packet's item 4 says HIGH-VALUE should be "resolved once at file-open/first-use against the effective sequence," while item 6 says the file's sequence governs. Two DIFFERENT sequences are in play and the spec separates them cleanly: §8.3.3.6.4 GR6 fixes the figurative's VALUE from the PROGRAM collating sequence ("otherwise, the alphanumeric program collating sequence is used"; LC_COLLATE when in effect for the program sequence), while §12.4.5.6.4 GR4 / REWRITE GR24 / WRITE GR35 fix the EQUALITY TEST to the FILE's (per-key, §12.4.5.7) sequence. Both must be modeled independently.

(e) C4 side-note. I verified §13.18.40.3 SR9 verbatim; the packet's critique is correct — SR9 is a class constraint, and the standard's explicit prohibition formula (present at §8.3.3.6.3 SR2: "shall be neither a figurative constant nor a zero-length literal") is absent there. I concur that the reject rests on taxonomy inference, and that C4 has no LENGTH fork either way.
second.answer:
I AGREE with the adjudication: SPEC-RESOLVED in favor of §8.3.3.6.4 GR2 (replicate the figurative to the key's length). But I reached it by a stronger route than the packet did, and I found four defects in the packet that must be corrected before it is acted on.

What independently convinced me is NOT NOTE 1 alone (the packet's sole load-bearing argument, which is vulnerable to the counter-reading that GR2's first conjunct demands an explicit statement-local length rule). It is this: I searched the whole of §14.9.25 MOVE and found that MOVE contains NO rule specifying a figurative constant's length — it defers to "the rules for figurative constants." If GR2's conjunct (i) required an explicit context-local length rule, then MOVE — NOTE 1's own first exemplar — would fall to GR3b, and MOVE HIGH-VALUES TO PIC X(4) would yield 0xFF plus three spaces. GR2 would describe the empty set. Conjunct (i) therefore means "the context supplies a length," conjuncts (i) and (ii) are jointly discriminating, and NOTE 1's placement under GR2 (physically between GR2 and GR3 in the source) settles that a comparison is such a context. SUPPRESS WHEN is a comparison (§12.4.5.6.4 GR6; REWRITE GR24; WRITE GR35) against an item guaranteed fixed-length (SR3). GR2 fires; GR3's protasis is false.

Concretely: SUPPRESS WHEN HIGH-VALUE against a PIC X(4) alternate key means a 4-character suppression value of the runtime high-value character repeated 4 times, compared under §8.8.4.2.7(1) equal-length comparison using the FILE's collating sequence. The 0xFF-plus-three-spaces outcome never occurs.

CORRECTIONS TO CARRY FORWARD (the packet is right in verdict, wrong in these details):
1. Re-cite GR24 as §14.9.35 REWRITE GR24, not §12.4.5.6.4 GR24 (§12.4.5.6.4 has only 6 GRs).
2. Add §14.9.51 WRITE GR41 and GR35 — the WRITE-side suppression rules the packet omitted; GR35 is the strongest single corroboration.
3. DO NOT assert on the §8.8.4.2.7(2) unequal-length branch. SR7 imposes no length requirement on a non-figurative literal-1, so SUPPRESS WHEN "AB" on PIC X(4) is legal and MUST space-extend. The equal-length guarantee holds only for figuratives.
4. Separate the two collating sequences: the figurative's VALUE resolves against the PROGRAM alphanumeric/national collating sequence (§8.3.3.6.4 GR6/GR7, LC_COLLATE-aware); the equality TEST uses the FILE's per-key sequence (§12.4.5.7, REWRITE GR24, WRITE GR35).

On C4: I confirm the packet's correction of the brief. §13.18.40.3 SR9 is a class constraint and does not contain the explicit figurative prohibition the brief attributed to it. Either way C4 has no length fork. No owner decision needed for C6B or C4.

When using that alternate key to access the file, the records suppressed would be skipped on reading the file and ignored when using the START statement." — whole-key match language, consistent with GR2 fill.

Annex E substantive-change item 42 (verified at line 50336, inside the Annex E span 49011–50351): "SUPPRESS WHEN phrase. The SUPPRESS WHEN phrase may be specified as part of the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause to suppress access to a record via a particular alternate record key when the value of this key equals the value specified in this phrase." — "the value of this key equals the value specified" is whole-key equality; confirms the feature is NEW in 2023 (also listed at line 1221 in the new-features summary), so VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE should carry it as 2023-introduced with no 85/2002/2014 behavior and no prior-edition fork.

I independently grepped the entire Annex D span for "SUPPRESS" and found only the single passage above — confirming the packet's claim that no Annex D worked example uses a figurative as literal-1. Neither annex contradicts GR2; both corroborate.

Also relevant and not an annex but informative: §14.9.30 READ ("any record identified as being suppressed ... is not considered to exist", line 29996) and the START rule (line 32191, "is ignored") confirm suppression is established only at WRITE/REWRITE and merely observed by READ/START — the packet's runtime scoping is correct.
second.implementationConsequence:
The packet's implementation plan is largely correct; adopt it WITH these four corrections (items 3 and 4 below are behavior-changing).

BINDER (ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause):
1. SR7 gate (unchanged): literal-1 must be an alphanumeric literal, a national literal, or a figurative constant, of the same category as data-name-1/data-name-2; if ALL literal, diagnose unless the literal is exactly one character. Note SR7 imposes NO length requirement on an ordinary literal-1.
2. Figurative expansion at bind time. keyLen = the fixed size of data-name-1, or for record-key-name-1 the sum of the sizes of all data-name-2 occurrences in SOURCE order (§12.4.5.6.4 GR2). SR3 makes this a compile-time constant. Apply §8.3.3.6.4 GR2: repeat the character value until length >= keyLen, then truncate from the right to max(1, keyLen) — i.e. replicate to exactly keyLen. Units are alphanumeric character positions for an alphanumeric key and NATIONAL character positions for a national key (§8.3.3.6.4 GR1). ALL literal-1 takes the same path.
3. CORRECTION to the packet — do NOT normalize an ORDINARY (non-figurative) literal-1 to keyLen and do NOT assert equal length at runtime. SR7 permits SUPPRESS WHEN "AB" on a PIC X(4) key; §8.8.4.2.7(2) space-extension governs it (key "AB  " is suppressed). Keep the unequal-length comparison path live; it is unreachable only on the figurative path.
4. CORRECTION to the packet — model TWO collating sequences, not one. HIGH-VALUE/LOW-VALUE resolve their character value against the PROGRAM alphanumeric (or national) collating sequence at runtime, LC_COLLATE-aware, per §8.3.3.6.4 GR6/GR7 — NOT the file's sequence. The suppression EQUALITY TEST then uses the FILE's per-key collating sequence (§12.4.5.7; §12.4.5.6.4 GR4; REWRITE GR24; WRITE GR35). Do not collapse these into one "effective sequence."

RUNTIME (WRITE and REWRITE only; READ/START merely observe — §12.4.5.6.4 GR6 NOTE, §14.9.30, START):
5. WRITE: per §14.9.51 GR41, for each alternate key whose value equals the suppression value, do not provide the access path and position the record so it is not found via that key.
6. REWRITE: per §14.9.35 GR24, handle both transitions — no-longer-equal ⇒ (re)provide the path and position the record to be found; now-equal ⇒ drop the path and reposition so it is not found.
7. Suppressed entries never raise a duplicate-key condition and never require DUPLICATES (WRITE GR41 closing paragraph; REWRITE GR24 closing paragraph — identical wording in both).
8. Cite §14.9.51 GR35 as the primary authority that all three of uniqueness, ordering, and suppression comparisons use the file's collating sequence per relation-condition rules.

CONFORMANCE TESTS (same commit, per feedback_conformance_tests_per_feature):
- SUPPRESS WHEN HIGH-VALUE on PIC X(4): key of 4x high-value IS suppressed; key of high-value + 3 spaces is NOT. This pair is the direct GR2-vs-GR3b discriminator.
- SUPPRESS WHEN SPACE on PIC X(10): all-spaces key suppressed.
- SUPPRESS WHEN ALL "0" on PIC X(6): "000000" suppressed; "0" + 5 spaces not.
- NEW, and missing from the packet: SUPPRESS WHEN "AB" on PIC X(4) — the ORDINARY-literal unequal-length case. Key "AB  " MUST be suppressed (§8.8.4.2.7(2)). This test is what prevents the packet's erroneous "assert on the padding branch" from shipping.
- National key with SUPPRESS WHEN SPACE: replication counted in national character positions, not bytes; comparison per §8.8.4.2.9.
- A key-level COLLATING SEQUENCE (§12.4.5.7 Format 2) case proving the equality test uses the FILE/key sequence while HIGH-VALUE's value comes from the program sequence.
- REWRITE transitions in both directions verified through subsequent READ NEXT / START on that key of reference.
second.confidence:
High on the classification and the answer for C6B — higher than the packet's own support warrants, because I found an argument the packet lacked. The packet rests almost entirely on NOTE 1, which a determined opponent can attack by reading GR2's first conjunct as demanding an explicit statement-local length rule. That attack is closed decisively by the fact that §14.9.25 MOVE contains no such rule and defers to "the rules for figurative constants" — so the strict reading would make GR2 describe the empty set and would break MOVE HIGH-VALUES TO PIC X(4) across all four editions. With that, plus NOTE 1's verified placement under GR2, GR3's receiver-less sub-rules, SR3's fixed-length guarantee, SR7's ALL-one-character restriction being coherent only under GR2, the WRITE/REWRITE explicit-override pattern, and Annex D/E whole-key language, I would not spend an owner decision on this.

Medium-high confidence that my four corrections matter operationally. Correction 3 (the unequal-length branch must stay live for ordinary literals) is the one I am most confident is a real latent defect in the packet's plan — SR7 demonstrably imposes no length requirement on a non-figurative literal-1, and the packet's "assert, not a code path" instruction would have shipped a wrong-behavior guard. Correction 4 (two distinct collating sequences) is textually clear but I have not traced how the existing file subsystem models the program-vs-file sequence split, so the integration cost is unknown.

Medium confidence on the C4 companion point, matching the packet: the SR9-based reject is an inference from the §8.3.3 taxonomy and SR7's own three-way enumeration, not a quoted prohibition, and §8.3.3.6.3 SR1 cuts the other way. I verified SR9's text and confirm it lacks the standard's explicit "shall be neither a figurative constant nor..." formula. Worth restating the diagnostic's justification, but C4 needs no owner decision either way.

resolved.fork: C5-fork1-FINALLY-on-fatal-path — does FINALLY run on the fatal/unhandled path?
resolved.readersAgreed: YES — both classify SPEC-RESOLVED, same six-case table, same emitter shape. The second reader added one normative-defect finding and two emitter details.
resolved.resolvingRule: §14.9.28.4 GR16: "If the FINALLY phrase is specified, the end of the PERFORM statement begins at imperative-statement-5" (with NOTE 8: "The end of the PERFORM statement includes the statements in a FINALLY phrase, if it is specified."). FINALLY has NO unwind semantics — it runs if and only if control reaches the end of the PERFORM. GR20 routes the fatal case to §14.6.13.1.3, never to the end of the PERFORM; item 4 there ends "Execution of the last imperative statement is terminated abnormally as specified in 14.6.12". Annex D.16.5 states it outright: "exception fatal: run unit terminates" sits at the end of WHEN COMMON, with FINALLY annotated "come here for no matching exceptions of if an EXIT PERFORM was in a WHEN".
resolved.behavior: Emit FINALLY as PLAIN SEQUENTIAL CODE at the tail of the PERFORM, NOT a C# `finally`/`try-finally`. Full case table: (i) normal completion ⇒ RUNS. (ii) caught by WHEN: nonfatal ⇒ RUNS; fatal ⇒ DOES NOT RUN (abend at end of last handler); fatal but the raising statement carries a non-NOT conditional phrase (ON SIZE ERROR/AT END/INVALID KEY) ⇒ demoted by §14.6.13.1.3 item 1 BEFORE item 4, WHEN is not even entered, FINALLY RUNS; fatal but handler executes RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT ⇒ RUNS; fatal EC-I-O ⇒ item 3 implementor latitude, a CONFORMANCE.md row. (iii) matched by no WHEN: nonfatal ⇒ RUNS; fatal ⇒ DOES NOT RUN (items 5/6/7). (iv) EXIT PERFORM from imperative-statement-1 or ANY handler ⇒ RUNS, skipping remaining handler phrases including WHEN COMMON; EXIT PERFORM inside FINALLY ⇒ lands AFTER END-PERFORM; GO TO out of range / GOBACK / EXIT PROGRAM / STOP RUN / propagated exception ⇒ DOES NOT RUN (NOTE 9 contemplates exactly this and only ADVISES against it).
resolved.implementationConsequence: L_FINALLY label after the handler phrases; fall-through from imperative-statement-1 lands on it. Fatal-handled path branches to abnormal termination, NOT to L_FINALLY. EXIT PERFORM lowering is POSITION-SENSITIVE: goto L_FINALLY from imperative-statement-1 or any handler; goto L_AFTER_END_PERFORM from inside FINALLY. FOUR ADDITIONS from the re-read: (A) §14.9.28.4 GR18 is a NORMATIVE DEFECT — it contains two consecutive conflicting sentences; sentence 1 says after WHEN OTHER "control is passed to the end of the PERFORM statement" (which by GR16 means FINALLY runs, fatal or not), and sentence 2's cross-reference to "General rule 14.9.29" is malformed (14.9.29 is the RAISE clause, not a general rule; the parallel GR17 and GR19 both read "General rule 20"). Implement GR18 AS GR20 (fatal after WHEN OTHER ⇒ abend, not FINALLY) and record a CONFORMANCE.md spec-defect row, or a future reader will "fix" the emitter back to the wrong behavior. Golden: fatal + WHEN OTHER + NO WHEN COMMON ⇒ abend, FINALLY marker absent. (B) RESUME in a WHEN SKIPS WHEN COMMON — RESUME is an unconditional transfer of control executed before GR19 can route to imperative-statement-4. Golden: WHEN EC-SIZE with RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT plus a marker-printing WHEN COMMON ⇒ COMMON marker ABSENT, FINALLY marker PRESENT. (Annex D.16.5's second listing still shows a WHEN COMMON block, which is boilerplate and easy to misread.) (C) GR14's implicit POP ALL / TURN OFF is sited "immediately preceding the END PERFORM phrase" — i.e. AFTER imperative-statement-5 — so FINALLY executes with WHEN checking STILL ENABLED; verify the emitter does not hoist the POP to the top of the tail block. That fixed textual siting is also independent structural evidence against protected-region semantics. (D) Honour the item-1 demotion UPSTREAM in the raise path — if C5 branches on Table 13 fatality BEFORE checking for a handling non-NOT conditional phrase, that is a real defect. Keep the existing EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT golden (expect 'H','C', abend, neither 'F' nor 'AFTER'); drop the "pinned literal reading — see openQuestions" framing in docs/rearchitecture/evidence/PHASE-13-grammar-batch-research.json and close the openQuestion — this is derived, not pinned.

resolved.resolvingRule: §8.3.3.6.4 GR2 NOTE 1: "A figurative constant is associated with a data item or literal when, for example, the figurative constant is moved to it, compared with it, or paired with it in a binary operation." — placed physically between GR2 and GR3, so a COMPARISON is a GR2 context by construction. §12.4.5.6.4 GR6 frames suppression as a comparison ("...is equal to literal-1"), and §12.4.5.6.3 SR3 guarantees the item is fixed-length. genuineForks.fork: C5-fork2-interior-TURN-legality — is a >>TURN directive legal INSIDE an exception-checking (format 3) PERFORM?
genuineForks.bareQuestion: Should the compiler emit a diagnostic for a >>TURN directive written inside imperative-statement-1 of an exception-checking PERFORM?
genuineForks.readingA: NARROW (first reader). §7.3.25.3 SR5 says "A TURN directive shall not be specified within an exception PROCESSING PERFORM statement", while the sibling PUSH/POP bans (§7.3.20.3 SR4, §7.3.22.3 SR4) both say "exception CHECKING PERFORM statement". §3.70 defines "exception processing procedures" as "procedures within WHEN phrases within an exception-checking PERFORM statement" — so "exception processing" names the HANDLER region and is expressly contrasted with the containing statement. SR5 therefore bans >>TURN only in WHEN / WHEN OTHER / WHEN COMMON / FINALLY. This is mechanically motivated: GR14's implicit PUSH ALL + TURN OFF ALL … POP ALL bracket spans exactly the handler region, so a >>TURN written inside it is unwound before END-PERFORM and has no surviving effect — precisely what a syntax rule should forbid — whereas a >>TURN in imperative-statement-1 sits outside the bracket and the standard specifies both its effect (GR14 s.4) and its survival (GR22). ⇒ ACCEPT silently in imperative-statement-1.
genuineForks.readingB: FLAT (second reader). "An exception processing PERFORM statement" is grammatically a KIND of statement (head noun "PERFORM statement" under an indefinite article), not a region within one. Decisively, the phrase occurs exactly TWICE in the whole document, and the other occurrence — Annex D.16.4, "The use of PUSH and POP compiler directives allows manipulation of the TURN directives, but they shall not be specified within an exception-processing PERFORM statement" — applies it to the PUSH/POP ban, which is stated normatively as "exception checking" and which BOTH readers agree is whole-statement. So the two phrases are drafting synonyms, and SR5's only claim to narrow scope collapses. Reinforced by TURN's own GR5 ("If specified within a statement..."), which fixes "specified within a statement" as the standard's idiom for whole-statement lexical containment; by §5.3.2/§5.3.3 (syntax rules govern what may be WRITTEN; general rules define MEANING — GR14 cannot confer legality); and by §4.2.2, which requires only "a warning mechanism that optionally may be invoked by the user" for syntax-rule violations, so GR14 s.4 is NOT dead letter under the flat reading — it says what an accepted-but-warned directive means. ⇒ WARN (suppressible) in imperative-statement-1.
genuineForks.observableDifference: Only whether a program containing `>>TURN` inside imperative-statement-1 of a format-3 PERFORM draws a diagnostic. Under A it compiles silently; under B it compiles with a suppressible conformance warning citing §7.3.25.3 rule 5. RUNTIME BEHAVIOR IS IDENTICAL under both readings: both require implementing §14.9.28.4 GR14 sentence 4 (a >>TURN turning OFF checking for an EC named in a WHEN phrase suppresses that WHEN for statements lexically AFTER it inside imperative-statement-1), and neither requires rejecting the program. Both readings also agree PUSH/POP are banned flatly and that a >>TURN in a handler phrase is an SR5 violation. Low stakes — but it is a user-visible diagnostic, which is why it comes to you rather than being decided in the code.
genuineForks.recommendation: Adopt READING B (flat) — emit a SUPPRESSIBLE conformance warning for a >>TURN anywhere lexically within a format-3 PERFORM, imperative-statement-1 included, and still implement GR14 s.4's semantics for the accepted case. Use ONE shared lexical-containment predicate for TURN/PUSH/POP (singular-mechanism rule); do not build a second region-partitioned predicate.
genuineForks.basis: Reading A's entire case is a word-choice-is-deliberate argument, and it is falsifiable — it dies if the drafters ever use "exception-processing PERFORM statement" for a ban everyone agrees is whole-statement. They do, at Annex D.16.4, for PUSH/POP. That is a counterexample, not a competing preference, and reading A quoted that very sentence without noticing it. Reading A's other pillar — that the flat reading renders GR14 s.4 dead letter — is dissolved by §4.2.2: syntax-rule violations need only be surfaced by an optionally-invoked warning, so non-rejecting compilers accept the construct and GR14 s.4 does real work. Honest residual: D.16.4 is INFORMATIVE, and no normative sentence says in so many words that SR5 covers the whole statement; SR5's wording deviation from its siblings remains unexplained under B (synonymy) as much as it is over-explained under A (intent). Reading A's structural point about the GR14 PUSH ALL/POP ALL bracket is real and unrebutted. That is why this is on your desk. The risk is one-sided: a suppressible warning that cites the rule informs the user without rejecting their program — exactly the posture §4.2.2 prescribes — whereas silent acceptance of a construct the syntax rules forbid is unrecoverable information loss. Whichever you choose, record the rejected reading with its citation in the EC deep-dive so it is not re-litigated.

rollup.summary:
Five claimed forks, ten adjudications (each first-pass reading adversarially re-read). FOUR RESOLVED, ONE GENUINE FORK — and the genuine one is low-stakes and needs only a one-line owner call.

RESOLVED (implement per the cited rule, no owner decision): C4-fork2 (repeated IS-form character-1 is LEGAL — editing rules 3+5 partition character-1 so SR24 never reaches the IS form; SR25 independently makes SR24 count EDITING PHRASES, killing the fork twice over). C4-fork3(a) (one FOR phrase MAY carry both NEGATIVE and POSITIVE — settled by rendering the printed Format 1 figure at 600 dpi, which shows the §5.2.6.4 choice-indicator bars the repo OCR dropped). C4-fork3(b) (the IS form NEVER floats, the FOR form DOES — editing rule 6's closed floating-symbol list, proved selective by CR/DB's absence). C5-fork1 (FINALLY does NOT run on the fatal path — GR16 makes FINALLY definitionally the end of the PERFORM, and it runs iff control reaches there; emit plain sequential code, never a C# `finally`). C6B (a figurative SUPPRESS WHEN literal replicates to the key's length per GR2 — closed by the fact that MOVE itself has no statement-local length rule, so the strict counter-reading would make GR2 the empty set).

The two readers reached OPPOSITE legality answers and both readings are defensible from quoted text — the disagreement is real, not an artifact.
